title.en: Founder of collapsed Chinese property giant Evergrande sentenced to life in prison
title.zh: 倒闭的中国房地产巨头恒大创始人被判无期徒刑

summary.en: Hui's sentencing marks a key moment in the fallout from Evergrande's collapse, which shook China's property sector.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The founder of Evergrande, the property giant at the centre of China's housing market slump, has been sentenced to life in prison and had all of his personal property confiscated.

Hui Ka Yan pleaded guilty in April to several charges, including embezzlement of assets and corporate bribery.

Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court also fined his former companies a total of 15.82 yuan (£1.73bn; $2.35bn) over multiple crimes, including falsifying records and concealing debt, according to state media.

Hui's sentencing marks a key moment in the fallout from Evergrande's collapse, which shook China's property sector and hit investors and domestic banks hard.

The court heard that Hui and his businesses "seriously disrupted" the Chinese property market, resulting in significant economic losses, state-controlled Xinhua News Agency reported.

Other Evergrande executives, including Hui's two sons Xu Zhijian and Xu Tenghe, were also sentenced to jail terms ranging from 22 months to 18 years, Xinhua said.

Once ranked Asia's richest man, Hui has seen his wealth and influence dwindle as his company unravelled.

Hui, also known as Xu Jiayin, rose from humble beginnings in rural China, where he was raised by his grandmother before venturing into property development and setting up Evergrande in 1996.

He oversaw the company's rapid rise through an aggressive expansion programme funded with large amounts of borrowed money.

Evergrande became China's biggest real estate developer, with a stock market valuation of more than $50bn (£36.7bn). Hui was once estimated to be Asia's richest person .

The firm was dealt a huge blow when Beijing introduced measures in 2020 to control debt in the country's property sector.

As the company struggled to meet interest payments on its debts it sold properties at huge discounts to stay afloat before collapsing in 2021.

In April, the court heard that the company had taken millions of dollars in pre-sale funding from potential house buyers that were not used for construction.

The money had instead been channelled to new property developments, resulting in hundreds of unfinished projects.

In March 2024, Hui was fined $6.5m and banned from China's capital market for life for his company overstating its revenue by $78bn .

Evergrande's stock market valuation shrank by 99% before its shares were removed from the Hong Kong exchange in August 2025 after more than a decade and a half of trading.

Evergrande's implosion has often been blamed for triggering a broader slump in China's property market that continues to weigh heavily on the economy.

At its height, Evergrande was the biggest firm in the country's real estate industry, which made up about a third of China's gross domestic product at the time.

body.en: A ‘capacity for despair’ forged by political oppression has long been consider a Magyar national trait. But after Orbán, writers in the country remind us that melancholy must not always be bleak A lone visitor looks for a garden outside an empty monastery. A morose housekeeper won’t let anyone behind the door of her own home. A retired general living alone on a crumbling estate waits 40 years to confront the only friend he ever had. Melancholy, an affinity with oblivion without a concrete cause, suffuses the Hungarian fiction translated for foreign audiences over the past 30 years, from the tortured tales of Sándor Márai to the taut novels of Magda Szabó. In his book In Praise of Melancholy, essayist László F Földényi tells the story of an Englishman who monomanically decides to teach himself Hungarian. For Földényi, the commitment to studying a language with 26 cases and with no connection to any other language, from a culture besieged by centuries of invasion, is to embrace melancholy, a seductive “capacity for despair”. To read Hungarian literature as an outsider, the poet János Pilinszky claimed in 1972, is to acquire unique spiritual insights that come from centuries of rootlessness, alienation and strife. title.en: Missing teen hiker found dead in Australian bush after eight-day search
title.zh: 失踪的青少年徒步旅行者在澳大利亚丛林中被发现死亡，搜寻持续八天

summary.en: Lily Hooper, a teenage hiker, was found dead in a Sydney national park after an eight-day search. She had been reported missing on August 12 after failing to return from a hike.
summary.zh: 莉莉·胡珀（Lily Hooper）在悉尼国家公园徒步旅行后失踪，经过八天的搜寻，这名青少年徒步旅行者被发现死亡。她于8月12日被报失踪。

body.en:
The body of a woman has been found in Australian bushland, following an eight-day search for a Sydney teenager reported missing last Wednesday.

Police said that while the body was yet to be formally identified, it was believed to be that of 18-year-old Lily Hooper. The confirmation came after the state premier told the New South Wales parliament that she had been found alive before later retracting the statement.

The teenager left her home in Sydney to go walking in a nearby national park on 12 August. Her family reported her missing later that night, after she failed to return home by 10pm.

Her car was found in a car park at the bottom of a challenging trail in the Nattai National Park.

Police said that the body was found in the Southern Highlands at approximately 11:30 local time on Thursday. Hooper's body had been found in dense vegetation and would likely have to be carried out on foot.

There was initial confusion as to Hooper's condition, after New South Wales Premier Chris Minns told a parliamentary hearing that she had been found alive. Local media suggested that her family had also been informed that she was alive.

Minns corrected himself shortly afterwards, and told the hearing that "Lily's body has been found" and she was deceased.

"This is obviously devastating, and I'm profoundly sad for her family and for all those concerned," said Minns, and apologised to the committee.

In a press conference on Thursday afternoon, Assistant Police Commissioner Joseph Cassar did not directly respond to questions as to how Hooper's family came to be told she had been found alive.

He told reporters that there was a period of between eight to 10 minutes before the teenager's parents were given an updated report on her condition.

He said he did not know exactly what was said to the Hooper family, but that if he "could turn the clock back, I would certainly".

A multi-agency search for the missing bushwalker had taken place over the past week, with support from multiple NSW Police Force units including PolAir, the Rescue Unit, the Trail Bike Unit, the Mounted Unit and the Dog Unit.

Police have also been supported by the Rural Fire Service, the National Parks and Wildlife Service and almost 100 members of the Australian Defence Force.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese paid tribute to the 18-year-old in parliament, calling Hooper's death an unspeakable tragedy.

"Lily Hooper had so much more to offer the world. Her passing, I have no doubt, will be felt very deeply," he said.

reflection.en: The tragic news of a young life lost after an extensive search brings profound sorrow. In moments of such deep grief, the shortest verse in the Bible reminds us that even Yahweh, in His humanity, wept at the death of a friend. summary.en: With the ruling party holding more than a two-thirds majority in parliament, the veteran BNP politician is expected to secure the largely ceremonial presidency.

body.en:
With the ruling party holding more than a two-thirds majority in parliament, the veteran BNP politician is expected to secure the largely ceremonial presidency.

Bangladesh's parliament is set to elect the country's new president on Thursday, with the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party's (BNP) Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir widely expected to win.

The BNP holds more than a two-thirds majority in parliament, making it unlikely that retired army officer-turned-politician Oli Ahmed of the opposition Jamaat-e-Islami-led alliance will get the vote.

The election comes after former president Mohammed Shahabuddin, a close ally of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina , resigned in July citing health concerns.

In February, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's BNP won a landslide victory in the first election since Hasina's 2024 ouster.

The party is expected to use its majority to hand the 78-year-old Alamgir the largely ceremonial presidency.

"I never thought that I would become the president, it is the infinite grace of the party and almighty Allah," he told reporters on Tuesday, according to the state news agency BSS.

"Even after becoming president, I wish to remain beside the people and serve them."

Alamgir was repeatedly arrested under Hasina's government, facing dozens of charges he said were politically motivated.

He has been hailed in the media for "keeping the BNP organized and maintaining the party's political presence during difficult times," referring to Hasina's rule.

summary.en: Apartment blocks and warehouses were targeted in the "massive attack" on Thursday, according to the State Emergency Service of Ukraine.

body.en:
A wave of overnight Russian missile strikes has killed at least eight people in the capital Kyiv and the surrounding region, Ukrainian authorities say.

Apartment blocks and warehouses were hit in the "massive attack" on Thursday, according to the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (DSNS), while a children's hospital and school were damaged. At least 33 people were injured.

Authorities are working to rescue people trapped underneath the rubble of demolished buildings, with crews already pulling two survivors from debris.

Meanwhile, Romania said one drone crossed into its territory at the northern border with Ukraine triggering an air alert siren.

In the early hours of Thursday, "a drone entered Romanian national airspace, approximately 13 kilometres east of the city of Galați," the Romanian defence ministry wrote in a statement.

The drone crashed into "an uninhabited area", causing a small fire that was extinguished.

"No casualties or material damage were reported", the ministry added, noting that the initial alert had been lifted.

The Polish military also said it had begun "defensive air operations" to protect its airspace, with the country sharing part of its south-eastern border with Ukraine.

Kyiv Mayor Vitaly Klitschko said a children's hospital had been damaged in the overnight strikes, where windows were broken and cars set ablaze nearby. There was also damage at an educational institution, he said.

An industrial centre in the Solomyanskyi district, south-west Kyiv, was also hit by missiles, according to the mayor.

An attack in Brovary district of the broader Kyiv region killed one man and wounded another, Kyiv regional governor Tymur Tkachenko said.

The regional administration issued an alert earlier in the night warning residents to take shelter. It continued: "Air defense operations are possible in the area".

More missile alerts were issued from regional authorities throughout the night, citing warnings from the Ukrainian air force that missiles were flying towards the capital.

The Russian airstrikes cut power to thousands of properties overnight, plunging parts of the Kyiv region into darkness, with technicians racing to repair the damaged energy grids.

The Russian defence ministry claims to have targeted a drone component production facility and a munition depot in Kyiv, according to state-run media, although the claims have not been independently verified by the BBC.

Kyiv has been battered in near nightly-attacks in recent weeks, with some strikes resulting in dozens of deaths and serious injuries.

More than a dozen regions have been targeted across Ukraine over the past week, President Volodymyr Zelensky said, with Russia launching more than 1,550 attack drones, 1,560 guide aerial bombs and 62 missiles Ukraine.

title.en: Australia 'outraged' after Israel decides not to open criminal investigation into killing of aid worker in Gaza
title.zh: 澳大利亚对以色列决定不起诉加沙援助人员遇害案表示“愤怒”

summary.en: Australia's foreign minister expressed outrage and plans to summon the Israeli ambassador following Israel's decision not to prosecute those responsible for the killing of aid worker Zomi Frankcom in Gaza. The minister described the decision as "insulting."
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长表示，以色列决定不起诉在加沙杀害援助人员佐米·弗兰克科姆的责任人，澳方对此感到“愤怒”，并将召见以色列大使。部长称这项决定是“侮辱性的”。

body.en:
Australia's foreign minister has said she is "outraged" over an Israeli military decision not to launch a criminal investigation into the death of aid worker Zomi Frankcom, who was killed in an IDF strike.

Frankcom was an Australian aid worker with World Central Kitchen (WCK) who was killed in Gaza with six other colleagues by an Israeli airstrike in April 2024.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong said in a statement the decision "falls far short of the accountability we expect" and called in the Israeli ambassador.

After meeting Wong, Israeli Ambassador Hillel Newman defended the IDF and its investigation, saying "there was no criminal intention" and therefore "no criminal responsibility".

Three British nationals, a Palestinian, a Polish national and a dual US-Canadian citizen were also killed in the attack. The UK has yet to comment on the Israeli decision.

Speaking to reporters after meeting Hillel, Wong said there were still many "unanswered questions", including why if the first strike on the convoy was "a catastrophic error", two further strikes followed, just minutes apart.

She also said the removal of two officers from their positions and the reprimanding of three after an initial probe was "insufficient accountability" for the death of seven people.

Drone audio from the attack had still not been handed over despite requests from the Australian government, she said.

In its statement on Wednesday, the IDF said the presence of an armed guard with the convoy had not been flagged with it before the convoy set off, and that he was falsely identified as a Hamas fighter. It also claimed the convoy had deviated from the route that had been coordinated with the military.

Notwithstanding "serious failures" in the process that led to the killings, "the decisions of the commanders did not raise reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct," the IDF said.

In the same statement, the IDF also said it had also failed to find grounds for criminal investigation into the killing of four employees of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), who were killed in two separate attacks in November 2023 and February 2024.

In her earlier statement, Wong said the Australian government had learned of Israel's decision late on Wednesday night, adding that the outcome was "especially insulting" as it occurred on World Humanitarian Day.

"This is despite Israel Defense Forces admissions that the IDF strikes on Zomi and her colleagues' vehicles were the result of serious failures to follow IDF procedures, mistaken identification and errors in decision-making," she said.

Wong said the government would continue pressing Israel "for justice for Zomi and her colleagues".

title.en: Captured Ukrainian-born soldiers tell BBC why they fought for Russia
title.zh: 被俘的乌克兰出生的士兵告诉BBC他们为什么为俄罗斯而战

summary.en: Men born in Ukraine who fought for Russia are tried for treason, but at a prisoner of war camp in western Ukraine, many believe they were defending their homeland.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
In Western Ukraine, behind high walls and layers of locked gates, there is a camp full of men captured fighting for Russia.

Many of those crouching in the shade around the edges of the prison yard were recruited from big cities like St Petersburg and Yekaterinburg, not far-flung and poorer regions like at the start of the full-scale invasion.

Amongst them are soldiers from Ukraine itself: the men who went to war with their own country.

Interviewing prisoners of war is not straightforward: to be sure they are not being coerced, first and foremost, and then to assess how openly they are speaking in the circumstances.

But with no access to the military inside Russia, it is a chance to assess the dynamics of this war and explore what might motivate the men fighting it. That includes the Ukrainian-born soldiers, on Russia's side.

We gave everyone the right to refuse an interview and spoke to those who agreed far away from any guards, and without cameras. As well as several formal interviews, I was able to talk to prisoners directly, in Russian, in several locations.

Anton was 10 when his part of Ukraine's eastern Donbas region was taken over by forces loyal to Moscow.

In 2022, when Vladimir Putin escalated to all-out war, he turned 18 and signed up to fight immediately - for Russia.

"I don't regret my choice. I went to defend my land," Anton insists and tells me his friends volunteered, too. "Then you get the SMS messages. Dead, dead, dead."

Other prisoners say the same: that all those they went to war with have been killed.

They also say fewer people are volunteering to replace them, despite enormous sign-up fees, which suggests Putin's desire to avoid mass mobilisation could soon be tested.

When Ukraine captures its own citizens on the battlefield, they are put on trial for treason.

Officially, Kyiv still sees them as Ukrainian and treats Russia's control of their regions as temporary. But the reality on the ground is more complex.

"They're very pro-Russian, and their national identity is very blurred," is how Petro Yatsenko from Ukraine's coordination headquarters for PoWs puts it.

"I consider myself Russian. A country means nothing, it's all about nationality. All my family are from Russia. All my roots are from there," he says.

An entire generation born in Ukraine has now grown up under occupation, with Russian schooling and media fully controlled by the Kremlin. Both have portrayed the authorities in Kyiv as "Nazis" and illegitimate for many years.

Since the full-scale invasion, even more territory has been subjected to the same.

summary.en: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle will return to the UK after living in the US for over six years, according to reports. The former senior royals will reportedly live in a private residence.

body.en:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle will return to the UK after living in the US for over six years, according to reports. The former senior royals will reportedly live in a private residence.

Prince Harry and his wife Meghan are moving back to the United Kingdom more than six years after they stepped down from their royal duties and shifted base to the United States, British press reported late Wednesday.

According to The Telegraph , the Duke and Duchess of Sussex are planning to go to the UK within weeks and settle in a private, non-royal house reportedly outside London.

The couple's children Prince Archie (7) and Princess Lilibet (5) have already enrolled in a British school and will begin classes from September, the BBC and several other news outlets said in their reports.,

There is yet to be an official statement from Harry or Buckingham Palace, which historically refrains from commenting on speculation about non-working members of the royal family.

 Harry (41)  —  who is the youngest son of King Charles III  and Diana, Princess of Wales — married former US actress Meghan Markle (45) in 2018 amid a media frenzy.

At the time, Harry's marriage to Meghan, who is biracial, was seen as a sign of progress within the British royal family. 

The couple moved to California after stepping down from their duties as working royals in 2020.

The growing rift with the royal family  only worsened after Harry published his memoir "Spare".

Harry and Meghan have  frequently criticized  the monarchy and the royal family, including in a series of TV interviews and a Netflix documentary.

They said they left Britain to escape the restrictions of royal life. The couple has also called out palace officials for being insensitive to Meghan's mental health.

In an interview with Oprah Winfrey, Meghan accused an unnamed member of the royal family of raising concerns about how dark the color of her son Archie's skin would be when she was pregnant with him.

Harry's relationship with his father King Charles III and his elder brother and heir-to-the-throne Prince William saw a total breakdown in the aftermath of the couple's exit. It is understood that the royal brothers are effectively estranged.

Last year, Harry said he wanted to reconcile with his father, who is undergoing treatment for cancer.

Harry and Meghan made a brief trip to the UK in early July with their two children, during which they had a private meeting with King Charles.

It was the first time Archie and Lilibet met their grandfather since the 2022 platinum jubilee of late Queen Elizabeth II .

British media reports that King Charles only became aware of Harry's plans to move back to the UK on Sunday.

United States President Donald Trump says he ‌plans to meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, saying that the Asian ‌nation holds 57 "very powerful" nuclear weapons.

The remarks come as Trump ordered Pentagon officials to ‌cut short joint exercises with the South Korean military.

He wrote in a Sunday social media post that they sent a message to North Korea that was "totally inappropriate and hostile, to a Country that, as long as Donald J. Trump has been President, ‌has been unthreatening and ‌respectful".

During Trump's ⁠first term, Kim called Trump a "mentally deranged US dotard" and threatened that he had use of a "nuclear button" on his desk.

But the two leaders turned that tension into face-to-face meetings, including a brief exchange at the demilitarised zone between the Koreas in which Trump became the first sitting US president to step into North Korean territory.

The leaders' relationship cooled after the face-to-face meetings in 2018 and 2019 .

"I ‌know Kim Jong-un very well, and he's going to be fine as long as we have ‌a smart president," Trump told reporters during a tour of the helipad he is constructing on the White House's historic south lawn.

"I get along with him well," Trump said. "And you know what? The fact that I get along with him, that’s a very good thing, not a bad thing."

"He has 57 very powerful nuclear weapons They should have ‌never allowed it. If I were president, I wouldn't have allowed it. But he's got them," Trump said.

Trump's citing of a specific number of nuclear weapons held by North Korea was highly unusual.

There have been varying estimates by experts over the years on how many nuclear weapons North Korea has.

The US government does not publicly publish an official estimate of North Korea's nuclear arsenal, although a 2025 report by the Congressional Research Service cited non-governmental experts as estimating that North Korea has produced enough fissile material for up to 90 warheads but may have assembled approximately 50.

In June, the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute estimated that North Korea has "possibly assembled around 60 warheads, possesses enough fissile material to produce at ⁠least 30 more".

title.en: India 'Cockroach' movement takes aim at government schools
title.zh: 印度“蟑螂”运动剑指政府学校

summary.en: A student protest movement in India, dubbed the 'Cockroach' movement, is expanding its grassroots efforts into a nationwide campaign. The initiative aims to audit government schools that have been neglected and to pressure authorities to address these issues.
summary.zh: 印度一项名为“蟑螂”的学生抗议运动正将其基层网络发展为全国性行动。该运动旨在审计被忽视的公立学校，并向当局施压，要求其采取行动。

body.en:
The student protest movement is turning its grassroots network into a nationwide campaign to audit neglected government schools and pressure authorities to act.

The student protest movement in India known as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) scored a major victory in July after Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down following weeks of demonstrations in Delhi.

Now, the movement is aiming its campaign for accountability at improving India's government schools.

Last week on India's Independence Day, the CJP launched a nationwide campaign asking citizens to inspect government schools, document what is missing and pressure local authorities to fix basic facilities.

Dubbed "Fix the Schools," the campaign aims to mobilize citizens to identify problems locally and make them public.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke launched a campaign in the Indian state of Maharashtra from his native village in Hingoli district. He spoke with students and documented what he said were broken windows, lack of clean drinking water, missing classroom benches and unusable bathrooms.

"No matter which political party ruled, nobody worked for government schools in states. Now there is a need, and we can make them work by asking questions," said Dipke.

Government officials did not respond to DW's requests for comment on the CJP's accusations.

The CJP has prepared assessment forms that parents, students and residents can use to document issues with local government schools. They are being asked to record video evidence, complete the assessment and send the material to CJP.

The organization plans to compile the reports into a public record of neglected schools and use them to pressure local authorities to respond.

The CJP has said the campaign will focus on five basic requirements: functioning toilets, electricity, clean drinking water, classroom benches and the quality of midday meals.

One element is to publicly recognize village heads who improve their local schools. The CJP plans to use before-and-after evidence to highlight villages where conditions have improved.

The organization has set an initial target of auditing at least 100 rural government schools over the next two months and pressing authorities to act on the findings.

The youth-led CJP began in May as a campaign calling for accountability over a scandal involving a highly competitive university entrance exam. The news that the question sheet had been leaked ahead of the exam date in early May exposed long-running grievances over privileged access for some students.

Fueled by millions of young followers on social media, the movement soon tapped into wider frustrations over unemployment, shrinking opportunities and an education system many young Indians believe has failed them.

title.en: 'Power of the purse': What Trump stands to lose in US midterm test
title.zh: “钱袋子”的力量：特朗普在美国中期选举中可能失去什么

summary.en: As midterm primaries continue with elections in several states this week, analysts are predicting a shake-up in the political landscape, indicating potential shifts in influence for former President Trump.
summary.zh: 随着本周几个州中期初选的继续进行，分析人士预测政治格局将发生变化，预示着前总统特朗普的影响力可能出现转变。

body.en:
The 2026 United States midterm elections will be a crucial test of Donald Trump's political strength, with Democrats hoping to regain control of Congress and Republicans seeking to defy the historical tendency for a president's party to lose ground halfway through a term.

The November elections will determine control of the House of Representatives and could reshape the balance of power in Washington for the final two years of Trump's presidency.

The first midterm primaries were held in March and have continued in recent months, with Alaska, Florida and Wyoming holding their primaries this week.

For Democrats, the November midterms offer an opportunity to demonstrate that dissatisfaction with Trump can translate into electoral gains and to begin rebuilding the party ahead of the next general election in 2028.

For Republicans, the elections will test whether Trump's political strength remains sufficient to protect the party from the historical midterm backlash that has affected many previous administrations.

And for Trump himself, a Democratic-controlled House could mean substantially greater scrutiny, investigations and political resistance during the final years of his presidency.

Wesley Widmaier, a professor at the Australian National University Department of International Relations, told SBS News an overall loss for Trump would restrict his influence.

"The House controls the power of the purse and is where budgets originate in the American system. A Democrat win would mean a loss of a lot of control for Trump," he said.

Ultimately, the midterms could provide the clearest indication yet of whether the political momentum in the US is shifting away from Trump and the Republican Party — or whether Republicans can defy the historical pattern and maintain their grip on Congress.

Every two years, US citizens elect all 435 members of the House of Representatives, while roughly one-third of the Senate is elected.

The House of Representatives has the special power to initiate tax bills and to impeach officials, while the Senate approves presidential appointments, such as judges and cabinet members.

Unlike in Australia, voting in US elections is not compulsory, and midterm elections — those held between presidential elections — tend to have lower voter turnout and less media attention.

But Widmaier said they still have significance for US politics and decision-making.

Historically, the president's party tends to lose ground in the House during midterm elections, he explained.

title.en: Donald Trump says no Iran talks planned, shares map showing Hormuz as 'new US territory'
title.zh: 特朗普称未计划与伊朗谈判，并分享地图将霍尔木兹海峡标为“美国新领土”

summary.en: US President Donald Trump stated that no talks with Iran are planned, while also sharing a map that depicted the Strait of Hormuz as "new US territory." Iran has maintained its stance that it will not reopen the vital waterway unless the US lifts its blockade of Iranian ports.
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，目前没有与伊朗进行谈判的计划，同时他还分享了一张地图，将霍尔木兹海峡标注为“美国新领土”。伊朗坚称，除非美国解除对伊朗港口的封锁，否则不会重新开放这条重要的航道。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has said no talks with Iran are underway and none are scheduled, as he posted a map showing the Strait of Hormuz as a new US territory.

Trump has been pressing his threat to claim sovereignty over the crucial energy waterway as the nearly six-month-old Iran war grinds on with little sign of resolution.

Trump's envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner had said on Monday that the US and Iran were having "very positive and active conversations", but the president denied that was the case.

"There are no talks or conversations going on, or scheduled, with the Islamic Republic of Iran. The Naval Blockade remains in full force and effect," Trump wrote on his Truth Social network on Tuesday night.

"The Hormuz Strait is open and operating. All water mines have been removed or detonated."

US sources told the Agence-France Presse news agency there had been "positive" discussions with the Iranians, but added that Trump had decided to wait and asked his team not to engage until Iran was ready to make a deal.

In recent weeks, there has been a lull in fighting, though the United Arab Emirates has recently accused Iran of firing two ballistic missiles — which landed at sea — targeting "maritime navigation." Iran, however, denied firing a missile toward the UAE.

Soon after, the UAE announced that "in light of regional escalations" it was halting all trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran.

The UAE bore the brunt of Iranian missile and drone attacks in the first period of the war, but had not reported any attacks since the US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June that was meant to halt the fighting.

Earlier on Tuesday, Trump posted a map on Truth Social showing the Strait of Hormuz as a "NEW U.S. Territory".

Iran has effectively shut down the chokepoint , through which a fifth of the world's oil would usually transit, in retaliation for the war launched by the US and Israel in late February.

Trump revisited the idea again earlier in the week in comments to reporters in the Oval Office.

This is not the first time that Trump, faced with a foreign policy obstacle, has threatened to annex foreign territory.

Since returning to power in 2025, he has threatened to make Canada the 51st US state, seize Greenland and Cuba, and has even alluded to taking control of the Gaza Strip, without following through on any of these threats.

Before the Iran war erupted on 28 February, the Strait of Hormuz was an open waterway with free passage.

title.zh: 倒闭的中国房地产巨头恒大创始人被判无期徒刑

summary.en: Hui's sentencing marks a key moment in the fallout from Evergrande's collapse, which shook China's property sector.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The founder of Evergrande, the property giant at the centre of China's housing market slump, has been sentenced to life in prison and had all of his personal property confiscated.

Hui Ka Yan pleaded guilty in April to several charges, including embezzlement of assets and corporate bribery.

Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court also fined his former companies a total of 15.82bn yuan (£1.73bn; $2.35bn) over multiple crimes, including falsifying records and concealing debt, according to state media.

Hui's sentencing marks a key moment in the fallout from Evergrande's collapse, which shook China's property sector and hit investors and domestic banks hard.

The court heard that Hui and his businesses "seriously disrupted" the Chinese property market, resulting in significant economic losses, state-controlled Xinhua News Agency reported.

Other Evergrande executives, including Hui's two sons Xu Zhijian and Xu Tenghe, were also sentenced to jail terms ranging from 22 months to 18 years, Xinhua said.

Once ranked Asia's richest man, Hui has seen his wealth and influence dwindle as his company unravelled.

Hui, also known as Xu Jiayin, rose from humble beginnings in rural China, where he was raised by his grandmother before venturing into property development and setting up Evergrande in 1996.

He oversaw the company's rapid rise through an aggressive expansion programme funded with large amounts of borrowed money.

Evergrande became China's biggest real estate developer, with a stock market valuation of more than $50bn (£36.7bn). Hui was once estimated to be Asia's richest person .

The firm was dealt a huge blow when Beijing introduced measures in 2020 to control debt in the country's property sector.

As the company struggled to meet interest payments on its debts it sold properties at huge discounts to stay afloat before collapsing in 2021.

In April, the court heard that the company had taken millions of dollars in pre-sale funding from potential house buyers that were not used for construction.

The money had instead been channelled to new property developments, resulting in hundreds of unfinished projects.

In March 2024, Hui was fined $6.5m and banned from China's capital market for life for his company overstating its revenue by $78bn .

Evergrande's stock market valuation shrank by 99% before its shares were removed from the Hong Kong exchange in August 2025 after more than a decade and a half of trading.

Evergrande's implosion has often been blamed for triggering a broader slump in China's property market that continues to weigh heavily on the economy.

At its height, Evergrande was the biggest firm in the country's real estate industry, which made up about a third of China's gross domestic product at the time.

body.zh: 处于中国房地产市场低迷之中的房地产巨头恒大集团的创始人被判处无期徒刑，并被没收全部个人财产。 许家印四月份承认多项指控，包括贪污资产和企业贿赂。 据官方媒体报道，深圳市中级人民法院还因伪造记录和隐匿债务等多项罪行，对他以前的公司处以人民币 158.2 亿元（17.3 亿英镑；23.5 亿美元）的罚款。 许的判决标志着恒大倒闭影响的关键时刻，恒大倒闭震动了中国房地产行业，并对投资者和国内银行造成了沉重打击。 据国家控制的新华社报道，法院获悉，许和他的企业“严重扰乱”中国房地产市场，造成重大经济损失。 新华社称，恒大其他高管，包括许志坚的两个儿子徐志坚和徐腾鹤，也被判处22个月至18年不等的监禁。 曾一度被评为亚洲首富的许氏眼睁睁地看着自己的财富和影响力随着公司的解体而逐渐减少。 许家印在中国农村出身卑微，由祖母抚养长大，随后开始涉足房地产开发，并于 1996 年创立恒大集团。 他通过利用大量借来的资金进行积极的扩张计划，见证了公司的快速崛起。 恒大成为中国最大的房地产开发商，股票市场估值超过 500 亿美元（367 亿英镑）。许氏一度被估计为亚洲首富。 当北京于2020年推出控制中国房地产行业债务的措施时，该公司遭受了巨大打击。 由于该公司难以支付债务利息，因此在 2021 年倒闭之前以大幅折扣出售了房产以维持运营。 4月份，法院获悉该公司从潜在购房者那里收取了数百万美元的预售资金，但这些资金并未用于建设。 这笔钱反而被用于新的房地产开发，导致数百个未完工的项目。 2024年3月，许先生因其公司虚报收入780亿美元而被罚款650万美元，并终身禁止进入中国资本市场。 经过十五年多的交易后，恒大股份于 2025 年 8 月从香港交易所退市之前，其股票市场估值缩水了 99%。 恒大的内爆常常被指责引发中国房地产市场更广泛的衰退，继续给经济带来沉重压力。 在鼎盛时期，恒大是中国房地产行业最大的公司，房地产行业约占当时中国国内生产总值的三分之一。 房地产市场是一个...

reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

body.en: A weak yuan guarantees Beijing massive trade surplus even as the White House tries tamp down on Chinese imports Since China offered a truce in the trade war last October following its threat to deprive the United States of rare-earth magnets, the Trump administration has been happy to stop escalating. After all, imports from China have been falling, down by 40% in the year to June, compared with the same period in 2024. Best to declare victory and call it a day. But the US hasn’t won this battle – and there’s strong evidence to show it’s too chicken to really try. Continue reading...
body.zh: 尽管白宫试图限制中国进口，但人民币疲软仍能保证北京方面的巨额贸易顺差。去年10月，中国威胁要剥夺美国稀土磁体，并提出在贸易战中休战，特朗普政府很高兴停止升级。毕竟，来自中国的进口一直在下降，截至 6 月份的一年里，与 2024 年同期相比下降了 40%。最好宣布胜利并就此结束。但美国并没有赢得这场战斗——而且有强有力的证据表明，美国实在太胆怯，不敢真正尝试。继续阅读...

reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到管家责任、供应与公共福祉。1 Peter 4:10提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以服事邻舍的好管家心态来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for Yahweh, not for human masters.
verse.textZh: 无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给主做的，不是给人做的。

Chery, which makes the Jaecoo and Omoda car brands, said the launch of a new R&D site was “the next step in our long-term plan” for Britain as it also moves towards manufacturing its cars in the UK. For those who commit their endeavors to Yahweh, there is a promise that their plans will be established. This reminds us that all human work, when offered to a higher purpose, can find stability and...
reflection.zh: 奇瑞汽车在英国设立研发中心，标志着其在重大商业项目上的进一步规划和投入。对于那些将自己的工作交托给雅伟的人，经文应许他们的计划必能坚定。这提醒我们，所有人类的工作，若能献给更高的目的，就能找到稳定和方向。

verse.textEn: Commit to Yahweh whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.
verse.textZh: 你所做的，要交托雅伟，你所谋的，就必成立。

title.en: Shares in humanoid robot firm Unitree surge 600% on Chinese stock market debut
title.zh: 人形机器人公司宇树科技在中国股市首秀股价飙升600%

summary.en: Unitree, the world's largest manufacturer of humanoid robots, experienced a remarkable stock market debut in China, with its shares soaring by over 600%. The company's robots have gained international recognition through videos showcasing their martial arts skills and performances as dancers for pop stars.

body.en: Company’s robots have gained global fame via videos of them performing martial arts and as dancers for pop stars Unitree, the world’s biggest humanoid robot maker, has made a spectacular entry on to China’s stock market, with its shares surging by more than 600%. The Chinese company’s robots have gained global fame via viral videos of them performing martial arts , running at Olympic speeds and serving as backup dancers for pop stars. Continue reading...
body.zh: 该公司的机器人通过表演武术和为流行歌星跳舞的视频而享誉全球。全球最大的人形机器人制造商Unitree已大举进军中国股市，股价飙升逾600%。这家中国公司的机器人因表演武术、以奥运速度奔跑以及为流行歌星担任伴舞等视频而广为人知。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The spectacular market debut of a humanoid robot firm highlights the accelerating pace of technological advancement and the explosion of human knowledge. As we marvel at such innovations, we are reminded of the prophetic insight that knowledge would increase. This rapid progress calls us to seek Yahweh's wisdom for how to steward these powerful new...
reflection.zh: 人形机器人公司的惊人上市，凸显了科技进步的加速和人类知识的爆炸式增长。当我们惊叹于这些创新时，我们被提醒，先知曾预言知识将增加。这种快速的进步呼吁我们寻求雅伟的智慧，以负责任地管理这些强大的新能力。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: Best of 2026 … so far: Asian mothers, bad feelings: notes on an all-conquering stereotype – podcast
title.zh: 2026年最佳播客回顾：亚洲母亲、负面情绪：关于一个普遍刻板印象的思考

This week, from April: A certain image of the tiger mom – strict, cold and demanding – is ubiquitous in popular culture. Why? By Rebecca Liu. Read by Ginnia Cheng Read the text version here Support the Guardian today: theguardian.com/longreadpod Continue reading...
body.zh: 8 月的每周三和周五，我们将发布一些我们最喜欢的 2026 年音频长读物，以防您错过，并附上编辑团队的介绍，解释我们选择它的原因。本周，从四月开始：“虎妈”的某种形象——严格、冷漠、要求高——在流行文化中无处不在。为什么？作者：丽贝卡·刘。作者：Ginnia Cheng 阅读此处的文字版本 立即支持《卫报》：theguardian.com/longreadpod 继续阅读...

reflection.en: Stereotypes, like the "tiger mom" image, often reduce individuals to a narrow caricature, overlooking the rich complexity of their lives and experiences. Yahweh created every person in His own image, bestowing inherent dignity and worth that transcends any simplistic label. This reminds us to see beyond common assumptions and recognize the unique personhood...
reflection.zh: 刻板印象，例如“虎妈”形象，常常将个人简化为狭隘的漫画式描述，忽视了他们生活和经历的丰富复杂性。雅伟照着自己的形象创造了每一个人，赋予了超越任何简单标签的固有尊严和价值。这提醒我们要超越普遍的假设，认识到每个个体的独特人格。

verse.textEn: So God created mankind in his own image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.
verse.textZh: 神就照着自己的形象造人，乃是照着他的形象造男造女。

title.en: Pentagon threatens to cut federal funding to 30 universities over foreign academic partnerships
title.zh: 五角大楼威胁削减30所大学的联邦资金，因其外国学术合作关系

summary.en: The Pentagon has threatened to cut federal funding to approximately 30 prominent US universities, including Harvard, Yale, and Stanford. This directive requires these institutions to review and sever foreign academic partnerships deemed a national security risk.
summary.zh: 五角大楼已威胁要削减包括哈佛、耶鲁和斯坦福在内的约30所美国顶尖大学的联邦资金。这项指令要求这些大学审查并切断被五角大楼视为国家安全风险的外国学术合作关系。

body.en: Harvard, Stanford and others face directive to review and cut alliances Pentagon deems national security risk Thirty US universities could lose federal funding unless they review and cut foreign academic partnerships the Pentagon considers a national security risk within the next two weeks, under a Pentagon directive aimed largely at ties to Chinese institutions. Harvard, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Johns Hopkins, Georgetown and Cornell are among the institutions ordered to conduct and report the reviews – and end partnerships deemed problematic – by 31 August, according to a US official who provided the full list to the Guardian. This article was amended on 19 August 2026 to remove a reference to Yale University in the subheading. Continue reading...
body.zh: 哈佛大学、耶鲁大学、斯坦福大学和其他大学面临审查和切断联盟的指令五角大楼认为存在国家安全风险根据五角大楼的一项主要针对与中国机构关系的指令，三十所美国大学可能会失去联邦资助，除非它们在未来两周内审查和切断五角大楼认为构成国家安全风险的外国学术伙伴关系。一位向《卫报》提供完整名单的美国官员表示，哈佛大学、麻省理工学院、约翰·霍普金斯大学、乔治城大学和康奈尔大学等机构被勒令在 8 月 31 日之前进行和报告审查，并结束被视为有问题的合作伙伴关系。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Major policy decisions, especially those impacting academic freedom and international collaboration, highlight the need for comprehensive and wise counsel. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us that safety and stability are found in an abundance of good advice, suggesting that broad perspectives are crucial when navigating complex national security concerns. May...
reflection.zh: 重大政策决策，特别是那些影响学术自由和国际合作的决策，凸显了全面而明智的建议的重要性。箴言11:14提醒我们，在众多的谋士中才有安全，这表明在处理复杂的国家安全问题时，广阔的视角至关重要。愿领袖们寻求多元的智慧，以确保决策能服务于所有人的长远利益。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: ‘Bad in every aspect’: derided low-tech animation Niu Lai rivals blockbusters at Chinese box office
title.zh: “各方面都很糟糕”：备受嘲笑的低技术动画《牛来了》在中国票房与大片抗衡

summary.en: A low-tech animated film, initially mocked for its crude quality, has unexpectedly become a box office hit in China, competing with major blockbusters.
summary.zh: 一部因粗糙质量而最初受到嘲笑的低成本动画电影，在中国票房意外走红，与大片竞争。

body.en: Commentary about the ‘so bad it’s good’ qualities of mother and son’s movie has driven people to see it at cinema A crude, low-tech animation about a cow and a skylark has become a sleeper hit at China’s box office, sitting alongside blockbusters such as The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day in cinema revenue rankings. Niu Lai, which translates to The Cow is Coming, is an 86-minute budget animation about a newborn calf and a skylark whose relationship develops over the course of an abstract dream sequence. Continue reading...
body.zh: 对母子电影“糟糕透了”的评论促使人们去电影院观看一部关于一头牛和云雀的粗糙、低科技动画在中国票房上取得了巨大成功，与《奥德赛》和《蜘蛛侠：崭新的一天》等大片并列影院收入排行榜。 《牛来》的意思是“牛来了”，这是一部 86 分钟的预算动画，讲述了新生小牛和云雀之间的关系在抽象梦境过程中发展的故事。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story reminds us that true worth and success are not always judged by conventional standards or initial human critique. Yahweh is the one who ultimately determines who rises and who falls, often surprising us with what He chooses to bless.
reflection.zh: 这个故事提醒我们，真正的价值和成功并非总是由传统标准或最初的人类评论来评判。雅伟是最终决定谁兴盛谁衰落的那一位，祂常常以出人意料的方式赐福我们。

verse.textEn: It is God who judges: He brings one down, he exalts another.
verse.textZh: 惟有神断定；他使这人降卑，使那人升高。

title.en: China’s economy showing signs that slowdown may be extending
title.zh: 中国经济放缓迹象或将延长

summary.en: China's economy is experiencing an extended slowdown, with industrial output and retail sales declining in July. This follows one of the country's weakest quarterly growth rates and increases pressure on Beijing for intervention.
summary.zh: 中国经济显示出放缓可能正在加剧的迹象，7月份工业产出和零售额均出现下滑。此前，中国经历了有史以来最疲软的季度增长率之一，这给北京带来了干预的压力。

body.en: Industrial output and retail sales slump in July after one of the country’s weakest quarterly growth rates ever China’s economy is showing signs of extending a slowdown with a slump in industrial output and retail sales in July, adding to pressure on Beijing to intervene with measures to support activity. After the world’s second largest economy posted one of its lowest quarterly growth readings on record in the three months to June, the latest figures suggest it continued to falter in July. Continue reading...
body.zh: 继中国有史以来最弱的季度增长率之一之后，7 月份工业产出和零售销售大幅下滑。随着 7 月份工业产出和零售销售的下滑，中国经济显示出持续放缓的迹象，这加大了北京方面采取干预措施支持经济活动的压力。在这个世界第二大经济体公布了截至 6 月份的三个月以来有记录以来最低的季度增长数据之一后，最新数据显示该经济体 7 月份继续下滑。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As a nation faces economic headwinds, it's natural to focus on policy and human intervention. Yet, this moment can also be a reminder that Yahweh is the ultimate source of our ability to create and sustain wealth. In times of plenty or scarcity, remembering His provision helps us anchor our hope beyond fluctuating markets.

title.en: Indonesia-China naval drill raises neutrality concerns
title.zh: 印尼与中国海军演习引发中立担忧

summary.en: Indonesia's participation in a limited naval exercise with China near Taiwan has raised questions about its long-standing nonaligned foreign policy.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚与中国海军在台湾附近举行了有限的海上演习，这引发了对其长期不结盟外交政策的担忧。

body.en:
Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill.

Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. 

An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy.  

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  

Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022.

Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training."

Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance.

"It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said.

However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan .

"Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said.

Kabinawa added that passing exercises were among the lowest-level naval activities yet used by China to justify its intimidation of Taiwan.

"Indonesia must also exercise caution in this regard," she said, adding that Jakarta should "not to be too naive," to assume that its participation in a "regular exercise" with China would not cause concern in...
body.zh: 印度尼西亚维持不结盟的外交政策，但雅加达有限地参与与中国海军在台湾附近举行的低级别海军演习，引起了密切关注。 8月12日，一艘印度尼西亚护卫舰短暂参加了与中国人民解放军海军在台湾东海岸附近海域举行的海军演习，台北向雅加达询问其参加演习的原因。 印度尼西亚海军护卫舰 KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai 与中国海军导弹护卫舰红河号一起进行了雅加达所说的“穿越演习”。这次演习是在台湾一年一度的汉光军演期间进行的。 印度尼西亚外交部发言人表示，他们完全意识到演习地点“使其特别敏感”，但强调其船只的存在“只是其返回印度尼西亚的过境路线的一部分”。据《台北时报》报道，这艘印尼舰艇在与俄罗斯海军演习后正从俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克返回。 中国8月11日宣布演习后，台湾陆委会谴责北京的“挑衅”。台北还要求外交部“提供更多细节”。 北京认为台湾是中国领土，并誓言要让这个自治岛屿与大陆“统一”，必要时会使用武力。特别是自美国前众议院议长南希·佩洛西 2022 年访问台北以来，解放军在台湾频繁进行军事演习，加大了对台湾的压力。 在台北和华盛顿的反应中，印度尼西亚海军表示，其与中国海军的活动“本质上不是战斗活动”，并且“无意进行战斗训练”。 台湾淡江大学国际事务与战略研究所副教授林英宇告诉德国之声，中国与印尼的演习没有什么战术意义。 他说：“这不像联合海上演习那么实际，但中国希望宣示其在该海域的能力。” 不过，日本国际问题研究所研究台印尼关系的客座研究员拉蒂·卡比纳瓦(Ratih Kabinawa)告诉德国之声，无论演习的意义如何，印尼都应该预料到台湾会做出一些反应。 “无论你喜欢与否，印度尼西亚现在都被拖入了这种地缘政治游戏，”她说。 卡比纳瓦补充说，此次演习是中国迄今为止用来证明其恐吓台湾合理性的最低级别的海军活动之一。 她说：“印度尼西亚在这方面也必须保持谨慎。”她补充说，雅加达应该“不要太天真”，认为参加与中国的“定期演习”不会引起人们的担忧……

body.en:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Opposition leader Angus Taylor have paid tribute to Lily Hooper after a body believed to be the Sydney teenager was found in the NSW Southern Highlands.

The 18-year-old left her home in Oakdale, in Sydney's south-west, at around 8am on 12 August to hike in the Nattai National Park. She was reported missing when she hadn't returned home by 10pm.

On Thursday 20 August, NSW Police said the body of a woman had been located in bushland at around 11.30am.

"While yet to be formally identified, the body is believed to be that of the 18-year-old woman," police said.

Speaking from parliament, Albanese said Hooper had been "taken from her family, the community and our nation far too young".

Police had found Hooper's car parked near the start of the challenging Bonnum Pic Walking Trail last Wednesday.

Hundreds of emergency services personnel have been involved in the search, including close to 100 members of the Australian Defence Force who joined the effort on Wednesday.

In state parliament, NSW Premier Chris Minns was informed during budget estimates that Hooper had been found, and initially announced that she had been found alive, the ABC reported.

"I apologise to the committee, but it seems as if the early advice was wrong," he said.

"This is obviously devastating and I'm just profoundly sad for her family and all those concerned."

He said in a follow-up statement afterwards that he had received incorrect advice and had "genuinely believed I was sharing good news".

"My deepest condolences are with Lily's family. I am profoundly sorry to think that anything I said may have added to their heartbreak at an already devastating time," the premier said in the statement reported by several media outlets.

On Tuesday, Hooper's family had issued a statement via NSW Police saying they were "absolutely devastated that our beloved daughter Lily is missing".

"We would like to thank all the emergency services and volunteers for their support and continued commitment to the search, not only during the day but throughout the night," the statement said.

"We desperately want to bring Lily home safe and we ask as the search continues, to keep our family and Lily in your thoughts.

"We also ask for privacy and understanding as our family navigates this unimaginable situation."

Liberal leader Taylor said the initial confusion over Hooper's condition had made matters worse.

"Lily loved bushwalking, and that only compounds the tragedy of her death," he said.

body.en:
More than 5.3 million Australians will receive higher social security payments within weeks under the latest round of indexation.

The new pay boosts will take effect from 20 September, increasing the rates of the pension, JobSeeker, Youth Allowance, Parenting Payment, ABSTUDY, and Rent Assistance payments.

"An extra $4 billion of cost-of-living relief will begin to flow to over 5.3 million Australians," Social Services Minister Tanya Plibersek said.

"Whether it's paying the rent, putting food on the table or covering everyday bills, this extra support will help Australians on income support make ends meet.

"We'll continue to make sure the system is there to support those who need it most, ensuring that everyone can make ends meet and no one gets left behind."

However, Cassandra Goldie, CEO of the Australian Council of Social Service, said that "while every extra dollar counts", routine indexation was not enough to lift people out of poverty and deprivation.

"People receiving JobSeeker are struggling to afford three meals a day and keep a roof over their heads," she said in a statement provided to SBS News.

"The government must deliver a significant real increase to JobSeeker, Youth Allowance, Parenting Payment and related supports so that people don't have to go without the essentials."

Social security payments are generally indexed twice a year to maintain their value and match changes in the cost of living and average wages. Here is how much each payment will increase by.

The maximum rates for age pension will be lifted by $36.80 to $1,237.70 a fortnight for single pensioners. Couples will receive a $55.60 increase to their combined fortnightly payment, bringing it to $1,866.00.

Pay rates for non-resident single pensioners will increase by $5 a fortnight, while partnered non-resident pensions will increase by $1.70 a fortnight each.

For singles without children who receive JobSeeker payments, the highest rate increases by $16.20 to $833.70 every two weeks. For singles with dependent children, the rate will increase by $17.30 to $892.80.

The rate for couples will rise by $14.80 per person, bringing the fortnightly payment to $763 each.

Parenting payment recipients will also see an increase, with maximum rates rising by $20.90 to $1,087.20 fortnightly for singles and by $14.80 to $763 for partnered recipients.

One million renters will also receive increased Commonwealth Rent Assistance rates.

body.en:
Foreign Minister Penny Wong has heaped further criticism on Israel, labelling its handling of the decision not to pursue criminal charges over the strike that killed Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom as "insulting".

Wong's comments came after she hauled in Israel's ambassador, Hillel Newman, for a diplomatic dressing-down after the federal government learned of Israel's decision hours after she launched the Zomi Frankcom award for aid workers at an event at Parliament House, attended by her family.

"Australia is outraged by the Israeli government's decision to not pursue any criminal proceedings against those responsible for killing Zomi Frankcom and her World Central Kitchen colleagues," Wong told reporters on Thursday.

"The Australian government learned of Israel's decision late last night, moments before it was announced on World Humanitarian Day.

"To learn of these developments in these circumstances was especially insulting and hurtful to Zomi's loved ones, to humanitarians, and to Australians."

Israel's military announced on Wednesday night it had completed reviews of 150 incidents of troop conduct in Gaza and made decisions on five cases, including the 1 April 2024 attack on an aid convoy that killed seven humanitarian workers , including Frankcom, in Khan Younis.

It said it had launched criminal investigations into two high-profile attacks on Palestinians during the war, but not into the April 2024 strike, adding there was "no ⁠reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct that would justify the opening of a criminal investigation".

Frankcom's convoy was marked, but the Israeli military initially claimed it was being used by Hamas, before later acknowledging the misidentification and errors in the decision-making process.

Two Israeli officers were dismissed from their positions and three senior officers were formally reprimanded, according to the Israeli military.

Wong said she had "made clear" to Newman "Australia's view that Israel's decision falls far short of the accountability we expect".

She said Australia's ambassador to Israel had conveyed the same message directly to Israeli authorities last night, including her foreign counterpart.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Israel had fallen short of the accountability required and the federal government would continue to press for justice for Frankcom and her colleagues.

body.en:
Australians are sitting on about $4.4 trillion in superannuation savings for retirement. But there are ongoing debates about whether they should be allowed to access some of that money early to help with costs of living.

And making an early withdrawal can have a big potential impact on your future retirement savings — especially if you are in your 20s or 30s.

So what are the rules around early withdrawal, and who do you have to convince if you're making a claim?

Superannuation savings are intended to help people cover their living expenses when they have left the workforce and are in retirement.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Taxes on super contributions are lower than income tax rates, and withdrawals after retirement are also at discounted tax rates.

Those low tax rates come with strings attached: rules that prevent people from using their superannuation savings for other reasons than income in retirement.

For the most part, superannuation savings in Australia are not readily withdrawn until at least age 60. People can withdraw super from age 60 if they have stopped working, or from age 65 even if they have not stopped working.

But the rules are strict. And who you need to apply to will depend on your reasons for seeking to withdraw money.

For instance, if you apply on compassionate grounds, you need to apply via the tax office and meet all of its criteria.

But in other circumstances, such as severe financial hardship, you need to apply directly through your super fund. Even if you meet all the criteria — which includes having received government income support payments for at least half a year — it's up to the fund trustees' discretion whether to say yes. The most you can withdraw for severe financial hardship is $10,000 in one year.

People often wish they could access their super for help with house deposits or home loan repayments. First home buyers may be eligible for the First Home Super Saver scheme. But in general, just needing help for mortgage repayments is not going to be sufficient grounds to access your super savings.

The tax office has had to issue warnings about misleading ads and social media claims, encouraging people to try to withdraw super on compassionate grounds, such as medical or dental expenses that are not absolutely necessary on health grounds.

The tax office says to be particularly careful with anyone suggesting super can be accessed to pay for cosmetic or elective procedures, as these treatments usually aren’t eligible.

If someone offers to help you apply to your super fund to take money out, that’s a red flag. It could even be a scam.

body.en:
At Steven Law's home in Northcote, Melbourne, family albums are strewn across the dining room table, offering glimpses into a past that was rarely discussed.

A large sepia photograph catches Steven's eye and he lifts a magnifying glass to look more closely.

It features a woman — Steven's grandmother Irene Law — wearing a large hat and a scarf draped around her shoulders. It is just the way Steven remembers her.

"Irene was an elegant woman; she was well spoken, well dressed. That was how we knew her," Steven told SBS Chinese.

Decades after her death, her image has appeared on walls across Australia, as part of artist Peter Drew’s Aussie poster series — bringing a little-known chapter of her life into view and raising questions about who gets to be called Australian.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

When Steven's sister Christina Law discovered that her grandmother would feature in Drew's poster collection, she was moved to tears.

"I was really overwhelmed and quite teary when I saw that nanna had been included in this series," Christina told SBS Chinese.

The posters feature archival photographs, sourced from the National Archives of Australia (NAA) of people who applied for certificates exempting them from the dictation test .

Under the Immigration Restriction Act 1901, one of the laws that formed part of what is now known as the White Australia policy, the dictation test could be administered at an officer's discretion to people seeking entry to Australia.

It required a person to write a 50-word passage in a European language dictated by an immigration officer. After 1905, the officer could choose "any prescribed language", making it possible to administer the test in a language the person did not understand.

People who failed were declared a "prohibited immigrant" and refused entry or , in some circumstances, deported .

The exemption certificates were designed to allow eligible non-European residents who had lived in Australia to leave temporarily and return within a set timeframe without being subjected to the dictation test.

The posters have since sparked mixed reactions, including graffiti, counter-posters and attempts to tear them down.

In recent months, videos of the artworks being defaced and altered to include different messages about identity have also circulated on social media.

"Someone has vandalised my old posters, so I've got some new ones, and I'm going to fix them up," Drew told SBS Chinese while standing on Morphett Street in Adelaide's central business district.

summary.en: The National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) in Australia is undergoing changes, prompting concerns that these reforms may lead some participants to feel like a burden.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚的国家残疾保险计划（NDIS）即将进行改革，引发了人们的担忧，认为这些变化可能让一些参与者感到自己成为负担。

body.en:
An overhaul of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) has passed the Senate with Coalition support, sent back to the Labor-controlled lower house to be rubber-stamped.

Analysis by the Grattan Institute suggests hundreds of thousands of people will be moved off the scheme or prevented from joining under the changes.

Applicants will be assessed in stages under a new test to determine their functional capacity.

That test is still being developed and will replace the current diagnosis-based model.

Acting CEO of peak body People With Disability Australia Megan Spindler-Smith says her community is grieving.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"There will be harm, there will be injuries. What we're talking about here is that when you reduce people's access to the supports that they need to be able to get out of bed, access the community, go to work, you ostensibly isolate people."

She says many lives will be made smaller by the reforms — which will slash social and community participation supports in half.

"The support needs don't go away when the funding is cut or when the supports are removed. They just get pushed onto either systems or other people, and that means isolation."

Since it started in 2013, the cost of the scheme has ballooned, rising to $50 billion dollars this year, and projected to hit $100 billion within a decade.

The government says its overhaul will slow the scheme’s growth and save almost $38 billion over the next four years.

Greens MPs like Jordon Steele-John say the focus on financial cost has made many disabled people feel like a burden.

“Many people, during the course of this debate, while the government has been trying to push this legislation through, have shared with me that they have felt as though they are being talked about in a way that leaves them feeling like a burden, and that is just not okay.”

Health Minister Mark Butler says reining in spending growth was necessary to safeguard the scheme's financial sustainability and social license.

"This plan puts the scheme back on track, and I'm confident, secures it for decades to come," Butler said.

"It genuinely has transformed the lives of hundreds of thousands of people, and I want to continue to see that happen for decades to come. title.en: Why a 52-metre SpaceX rocket ended up off the coast of Christmas Island
title.zh: 为何一枚 52 米长的 SpaceX 火箭最终坠入圣诞岛海岸

summary.en: The rocket's arrival at the remote island caused a stir among the locals.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Elon Musk's aerospace company SpaceX has retrieved a rocket that splashed down in the Indian Ocean near Christmas Island.

The space debris was towed to the remote island, about 1,500 kilometres off north-west Western Australia, on Tuesday.

"After approx. 24 days at sea, the SpaceX Recovery team successfully guided Starship to a location just off the coast of Christmas Island," the US aerospace manufacturer and launch services company said in a social media post.

"A team of SpaceX engineers is on their way to conduct additional analysis on the vehicle in calmer waters before attempting to return it to Starbase."

Locals in the remote territory reportedly lined up along the rugged coastline to catch a glimpse of the 52-metre-long rocket as it was towed in.

Photographer Chris Bray, who usually focuses on wildlife, said it was not something he ever expected to see.

"This SpaceX Starship was towed into the protected waters around Christmas Island this morning after an unusually gentle landing in the Indian Ocean almost a month ago left it unexpectedly floating and potentially recoverable instead of the usual explosion!" he said on an Instagram post on Tuesday.

Bray's aerial photos show the mostly black-coloured rocket being towed by cable attached to two large ships.

The rocket, which has three large and three small rocket nozzles, appears to have lost some of its outer coating, but was otherwise intact.

The SpaceX website said the company's Starship spacecraft and super heavy rocket were a reusable transport system designed to carry crew and cargo into "orbit, the moon, Mars and beyond".

In 2023, a large gold-coloured dome-like object was found on a beach about 250km north of Perth.

The Australian Space Agency later concluded it was an expended third stage of a polar satellite launch vehicle operated by the Indian Space Research Organisation.

In 1979, parts of NASA's Skylab space station crashed to earth near the sleepy towns of Esperance and Balladonia, triggering a global media frenzy.

title.en: Criminal networks in crosshairs as Australia and Thailand deepen ties
title.zh: 澳大利亚和泰国加深联系，犯罪网络成为焦点

summary.en: From scam syndicates to fuel security, Australia and Thailand have mapped out a closer strategic partnership.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及合一、和好与弥合分歧。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The leaders of Australia and Thailand have agreed to step up joint efforts to tackle transnational crime, while also pledging to elevate defence and trade ties.

Thailand prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul, in his first visit to Australia since he became leader in late 2025, met with his counterpart Anthony Albanese in Canberra on Wednesday.

The pair agreed to bolster mutual commitments to handle transnational crime, including tasking their law-enforcement agencies to "disrupt increasingly sophisticated global criminal networks", they said in a joint statement.

The nations will also elevate their security relationship by committing to a biannual meeting of defence ministers.

In a boost for Australia's fuel security, Albanese said his counterpart had made the "generous offer" of access to jet fuel, as energy markets experience supply-chain shocks as a result of the US-led war on Iran.

"Building on the strong economic ties is a top priority for my government," he told reporters.

"Times of uncertainty call for greater global cooperation between partners who are reliable and dependable, and friends."

In 2027, Australia and Thailand will mark 75 years since diplomatic relations were established between the two countries.

Anutin said: "I'm confident that our strategic partnership will remain an enduring foundation for Thailand and Australia ... and bring our countries and peoples even closer together."

"I extend my sincere appreciation once again to my dear Prime Minister Albanese and the Australian people for their warm hospitality."

The bid to crack down on transnational crime comes after Thailand tries to alleviate its reputation for being a hotspot for grey money — illicit capital that crosses borders.

The nation is an international hub for online scam work which fleeces millions of dollars from Australians each year.

Vulnerable Thai locals are often imprisoned by criminal syndicates on the outskirts of Bangkok to run the centres.

The Australian Federal Police was involved in a 2025 investigation that led to the arrest of five Australians, as well as United Kingdom, Canadian and South African nationals, operating a scam Bangkok "boiler room".

That announcement also came hours after Thai police confirmed the cause of death of a Thai woman allegedly murdered by an Australian man in June.

The Thai teenager, Tunchanok Donhomla, was allegedly suffocated, according to a police autopsy report seen by the ABC.

Thai police told ABC News that, on the basis of evidence collected, they now believed the investigation was reaching its completion.
